study_identification.title: Normative modeling analysis reveals corpus callosum volume changes in early and mid-to-late first episode major depression

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate corpus callosum (CC) and subvolume differences (genu, body, splenium) between first-episode MDD patients and age- and gender-matched never-depressed healthy controls using normative modeling, and to examine whether early-onset versus mid-to-late-onset first depressive episodes affect CC subvolumes differently and whether depression severity symptoms correlate with CC subvolumes.

Supporting Text: A one-sample t-test on the resulting z-scores of first episode MDD patients was then performed to determine the statistical significance of the mean deviation (z-scores). Given the hypothesis of CC (sub)volume reductions, significance was set at p < 0.05, one-tailed. To evaluate the effects of depression severity, we computed three separate Spearman correlations between the HAMD scores and CC (sub) volume z-scores, 1) for the whole first episode MDD group; 2) at early onset (age ≤ 44y), and 3) at mid-to-late onset (age ≥ 45y). Medication (yes/no) was added as a covariate. This yielded 12 different correlations. Given the exploratory nature of these analyses, significance was set at p < 0.05, two-tailed. Type I error due to multiple comparisons across CC subdivisions was controlled using Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction.

clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed:
Answer: When examining the whole first-episode MDD sample (N=369), significant CC volume z-score reductions were found in the entire CC (t=-1.715, p=0.044, one-tailed) and in the body of the CC (t=-2.565, p=0.005, one-tailed, FDR corrected) compared to healthy control norms. No significant effects were found for genu or splenium in the whole sample. Depression severity (HAMD scores) did not correlate with CC subvolume z-scores in the whole sample (all p>0.05). When analyzing early-onset (age ≤44y, N=283) and mid-to-late-onset (age ≥45y, N=86) subgroups separately, mid-to-late-onset first-episode MDD showed significant CC volume z-score decreases for the entire CC (t=-2.102, p=0.019, one-tailed) and the body of the CC (t=-2.788, p=0.003, one-tailed, FDR corrected). In contrast, early-onset first-episode MDD patients did not show significant mean CC subvolume z-score differences from norms. However, in early-onset patients, depression severity (HAMD scores) was significantly positively associated with increased entire CC volume z-scores (r=0.152, p=0.011, two-tailed), body z-scores (r=0.147, p=0.014, two-tailed, FDR corrected), and splenium z-scores (r=0.140, p=0.019, two-tailed, FDR corrected), after controlling for medication status. No such correlations were found in mid-to-late-onset patients (all p>0.05). There were no significant differences in CC subvolume z-scores between early-onset and mid-to-late-onset groups (all p>0.05, two-tailed).
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative

clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Answer: Education was included as a fixed covariate in the normative model because the HC and MDD groups differed significantly in education levels, allowing the normative model to account for education effects on CC volumes. The study used the JHU DTI-based white-matter atlas for CC parcellation into three subregions. Medication status (yes/no) was included as a covariate in correlation analyses. The authors suggest that CC volume increases in early-onset MDD with higher depression severity may represent a compensatory neuroplastic response or inflammatory reaction (astrocyte proliferation) in response to stress. Behavioral analyses were performed in R language. The findings underscore the importance of prompt clinical interventions especially in early-onset first-episode MDD.

general_notes.general_notes: Data from REST-meta-MDD Consortium, a collaborative effort of 25 research groups from 17 hospitals in China. After quality control and exclusions, 490 healthy controls and 369 first-episode MDD patients from 7 study sites were analyzed. MRI acquisition parameters referenced to Yan et al. (2019). CC parcellation based on JHU DTI-based white-matter atlases into entire CC, genu, body, and splenium. PCNToolkit v0.18 used for hierarchical Bayesian regression normative modeling. Fixed effects: age, sex, education, total intracranial volume. Site modeled as random effect via hierarchical structure. No model validation metrics (EV, MSLL, skewness/kurtosis) reported. Supplemental materials include: Table 1 with summary of previous VBM studies on MDD and CC, meta-analysis forest plots (Supplemental Fig. 1), and age/education distributions (Supplemental Fig. 2). Study design cutoff of age 44y vs 45y for early vs mid-to-late onset based on Zisook et al. (2007). All MDD patients had HAMD ≥14 indicating moderate to severe depression. Early-onset and mid-to-late-onset groups did not differ in depression severity (HAMD scores, p=0.08) but differed in age (by definition), education (p=0.02), and medication status (p=0.015).
